- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.

I need to decide on a bid for an auction.

The Short Line railroad is up for auction. The current high bid is $36. I will bid incrementally to $99 and mortgage the property immediately upon winning. This maximizes cash flow.

I am weighing whether the Short Line is worth more than its $99 mortgage ceiling. I own two other mortgaged railroads, and p2 owns one.

I need to account for p2's dangerous monopolies. They own Orange and Dark Blue with heavy houses, plus Kentucky and Illinois unmortgaged. I must preserve cash to survive landing on their properties.

I will bid $37. The mortgage arbitrage still nets $63 if I win and mortgage the property.

Both players face the same mortgage arbitrage incentive up to $99. If p2 buys and mortgages, they profit too. The one who wins at $99 gains $1. The one who wins at $100 breaks even on mortgage. Above $100, immediate mortgage loses money. p2 might value the Short Line more if they want railroad rent. Their B&O mortgaged property costs $110 to unmortgage.

Railroad rent is too low to justify a large bid. I will drop out at $100 or higher if p2 continues. A jump bid would waste money if they fold.
